conventions.convention: Hilbert pairings are linear in the first variable. The integrated form uses fixed left Haar measure and the pairing integral ∫ f(g)〈π(g)ξ,η〉 dg.
Star-representations are bounded complex-linear maps. Nondegeneracy means the closed span of their action is the whole carrier; no algebra unit is required.
A state is a positive linear functional of norm one. The zero algebra has no state.
Weak containment π≺ρ tests every diagonal coefficient of π against finite sums of diagonal coefficients of ρ, uniformly on every compact set. Zero representations are allowed.
The kernel-inclusion direction is π≺ρ iff kerρ⊆kerπ. The homeomorphism is from the quotient by weak equivalence, not from the unquotiented unitary dual.
Spectra in a nonunital C*-algebra are computed in its minimal unitization; positivity starts algebraically as a*a.
KR uses Q[a,x_i], deg(a)=(2,0), deg(x_i)=(0,2), differential degree (1,1), and homotopy degree (-1,-1). Internal shifts raise generator degrees; parity reversal Π is separate from internal shifts.
The arc from x2 to x1 has row (a,x1−x2) and shift {-1,1}. Wide-edge outgoing labels are x1,x2 and incoming labels x3,x4; its quadratic zero-first-entry row has shift {-1,3}.
Positive crossings use C(Γ0){0,2}→χ0 C(Γ1) in outer degrees -1,0. Negative crossings use C(Γ1){0,-2}→χ1 C(Γ0){0,-2} in degrees 0,1.
For nonempty closed diagrams, take both inner-parity cohomologies and forget their parity labels before outer cohomology. The empty diagram instead has raw cohomology Q[a] and Euler series (1−t²)^−1.
Normalized v2 Euler series excludes empty closures, uses α=−t^−1q^−1 and exponent e−s+1, with a fixed formal invertible square root. Published regrading and Euler weights are distinct conventions.
Plancherel weights are (fλ)²/n! for n≥0, with f∅=0!=1 and P0(∅)=1. Positive-order normalized observables require n≥1.
Russian coordinates are x=s−r, y=r+s. The scaled profile is n^−1/2λ(√n x), with half the area between it and |x| equal to one.
Profile moments are k(k−1)∫x^(k−2)σω(x) dx for k≥2, with σω=(ω−|x|)/2 and p̃1=0. Shifted characters vanish when diagram size is below |ρ|.
Weight is |ρ|+ℓ(ρ), whereas Kerov degree is |ρ|+m1(ρ). Unique union top terms hold for weight; Kerov degree also permits inverse-cycle contractions.
ηρ divides pρ# by n^((|ρ|+m1(ρ))/2) and ∏k≥2 k^(mk(ρ)/2), using positive real roots on Yn and localization adjoining both square root and inverse square root of p1#.
The character CLT is joint convergence for each fixed finite N≥2. ηk=p_k#/(√k n^(k/2)) has standard-normal limits; p_k#/n^(k/2) has variance-k limits.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, with spectra in A or its minimal unitization, self-adjoint elements have real spectrum and continuous functional calculus; algebraic positivity equals nonnegative spectrum and gives a closed pointed convex cone; conjugation preserves order, positive order bounds norms, star-homomorphisms are contractive, unital star-homomorphisms preserve normal functional calculus, and functions vanishing at zero applied to nonunital self-adjoint elements remain in A.

Assume AC and G LCH. Every strongly continuous unitary representation extends uniquely to a nondegenerate star-representation of C*(G); every nondegenerate star-representation pulls back nondegenerately to L1(G). These give a bijection respecting unitary equivalence and irreducibility.

The pρ# have unique polynomial extensions to A=R[p̃2,p̃3,…] and form a linear basis. Both |ρ|+m1(ρ) and |ρ|+ℓ(ρ) define algebra filtrations; the latter is the profile-moment weight filtration and dominates the former. The product pσ#pτ# is pσ∪τ# with coefficient one plus strictly lower-weight terms.

The stated elementary Koszul row operation is an isomorphism, grading-preserving when homogeneous. If R=R′[y], the potential belongs to R′ and a row is (0,y−μ), restriction to R′ is homotopy equivalent to deleting that row and substituting y=μ everywhere else. A nonempty closed graph reduces to a universal (a,0) row and the remaining zero-first-entry Koszul rows; after restriction to Q its cohomology retains the universal odd parity and {-1,1} shift, and a acts trivially.

Assume AC and G LCH with fixed left Haar measure. On continuous positive-type functions normalized by φ(e)=1, convergence of every pairing ∫fφi for f∈L1(G) is equivalent, for arbitrary nets, to uniform convergence on every compact subset of G.

Assume AC and G LCH. If an irreducible π is weakly contained in a set-indexed direct sum of nonzero unitary representations ρs, each unit-vector coefficient is compact-uniformly approximable by one unit-vector coefficient of one ρs. Any finite list of vector coefficients can be approximated simultaneously in a single summand. If all ρs are irreducible, [π] lies in their Fell closure.

Assume AC and G LCH. For strongly continuous unitary π,ρ, π≺ρ, kerρ⊆kerπ in C*(G), and ‖π(a)‖≤‖ρ(a)‖ for every a∈C*(G) are equivalent. For irreducibles, mutual weak containment is equivalent to equality of kernels.
For every partition ρ of size r and every n≥0, EPn[pρ#]=n↓r when ρ=(1^r), and zero otherwise; when n<r both the observable and falling factorial vanish.

For m1(ρ)=0 and n≥max(1,|ρ|), ∏k≥2 Hmk(ρ)(ηk)=ηρ+Rρ exactly on Yn. Rρ is a finite sum cσ,j n^−j/2 ησ with j≥1, m1(σ)=0 and |σ|1−j<|ρ|1. Its expectation is O(n^−1/2); the Hermite product has that expectation for nonempty ρ and expectation one for empty ρ.

For a fixed interval I=[a,b], a≤b, and real 1-Lipschitz functions supported in I, every ε>0 admits finitely many polynomial moments and a positive threshold whose simultaneous smallness forces supremum norm at most ε. Polynomial-moment and uniform topologies coincide on this set.

Assume AC and d≥1. If all mixed moments of Rd-valued Xn converge to those of a Borel probability μ with finite mixed moments, and μ is determined among finite-moment Borel probabilities by them, then their laws converge weakly to μ. Every multivariate Gaussian law, including singular covariance, is moment-determinate.

Assume AC. Clockwise braid diagrams with admissible markings and ambient-isotopic oriented closures have isomorphic trigraded homology after an overall integer shift accumulated along a Markov sequence. Type IA contributes {1,1}[1] after inner parity is forgotten; type IB contributes none.

Assume AC and nonempty braid closure. Published correction is Cv2{r,r}[r], r=(s−e)/2; its parity-forgotten termwise cohomology is Markov invariant and its published Euler series is F/(1−t²). The v2 series is Markov invariant and satisfies F=(1−t²)tq F̃(−t²q,q). In the specified localization, the stated Hecke coefficient homomorphism gives F=δφ(P), δ=(t^−1−t)/(q−q^−1). Raw empty-diagram values are separately excluded from these HOMFLYPT identifications.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 ends 'hence the second bound with φ(e) in place of ‖ξ‖'. The preceding calculation actually gives the sharper bound sqrt(2φ(e)(φ(e)−Re φ(y))). Obtaining the stated sqrt(2φ(e)(1−Re φ(y))) requires explicitly using φ(e)≤1; replacing ‖ξ‖ by φ(e) is not the normalization identity. The claim is sound, but this closing justification needs clarification.

Proof 3.1, source line 79, contains '$R<TAB>o (x_4-x_2)R$' in 'the polynomial-subspace map'. The character after R is an actual tab (U+0009), followed by o, rather than the intended LaTeX arrow command. This is a presentation defect in the displayed map.
